_comment: preselect = what Legroom checks on its own, only in safety=safe rules: minAgeDays (nothing changed inside the item for N days), skipRunningApps (skips folders named after the bundle id of an open app), skipPrefixes/skipNames (never checked), minBytes (ignores small items). review/info rules are never prechecked.

title: Trash
why: What's already in the Trash still takes up space. Emptying it is the only permanent removal, so Legroom doesn't do it for you: open the Trash in Finder and empty it when you're sure.

title: App caches
why: Local copies apps keep so they open faster. Deleting them is safe; apps recreate what they need, so the gain may be partial.

title: Logs
why: Diagnostic records from your apps. They're only useful for investigating problems; deleting them is safe.

title: Saved window state
why: Window positions and contents used to restore each app when it reopens. Small, and harmless to delete.

title: Xcode builds (DerivedData)
why: Intermediate build results. Xcode rebuilds them the next time you open the project; it only costs time.

title: Xcode Archives
why: Builds archived for distribution, with debug symbols. Keep the ones for versions still published; delete the old ones.

title: iOS symbols (DeviceSupport)
why: One folder per iOS version you've connected to Xcode. Keep only the versions for devices you still use; Xcode downloads them again if needed.

title: Simulators
why: Each simulator is a complete iPhone with apps and data. Don't move these folders by hand: run `xcrun simctl delete unavailable` in Terminal, which safely removes outdated ones.

title: iPhone & iPad backups
why: Local backups made by Finder. Each one can be tens of GB. Before deleting, check in Finder › device › Manage Backups which one belongs to which device and date.

title: Attachments opened in Mail
why: Copies of attachments you opened from Mail. The originals stay in the messages.

title: Developer tool caches
why: Packages downloaded by npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, Gradle, Cargo, Maven, CocoaPods, and Homebrew. Everything is downloaded again when a project needs it.

title: Docker Desktop
why: Docker's virtual disk grows and doesn't shrink on its own. Run `docker system prune` and reduce the disk size in Docker Desktop settings.
